question: What is the typical temperature range of a mercury-based clinical thermometer?
solution:
The correct answer is __35°C to 42°C.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The typical temperature range__ of a mercury-based clinical thermometer is 35°C to 42°C.
 
• Mercury-based clinical thermometers are used to measure human body temperature.
 
• The range is designed to cover the normal and fever temperatures of the human body.
 
• These thermometers provide accurate readings due to the thermal expansion properties of mercury.
 
• They are primarily used in medical applications to monitor health conditions.
 
• Mercury thermometers have been replaced in many places by digital ones due to safety and environmental concerns.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Thermometers:**

 
 
• Digital thermometers are more commonly used today due to their safety and ease of use.
 
• They do not contain mercury and provide quick and accurate results.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Thermometers:**
 
 
• These devices use infrared technology to measure temperature.
 
• 
• They are contactless and are often used for measuring temperature from a distance.
 
• 
• Commonly used during pandemics for quick temperature screening.
 
 
 
• **Alcohol Thermometers:**
 
 
• These thermometers use colored alcohol instead of mercury as the liquid.
 
• They are safer but may not be as accurate as mercury-based thermometers.
